text:
ajay: Heads up — seeing big retry spikes and skewed traffic to a subset of endpoints for the gpu-serving service in us-west1-b, affecting inference tail latency.

maya: timeline? started after last night's capacity drain?

ajay: yup around 02:40 UTC after we drained a few older nodes for kernel patch. error rate jumped 4x, retries concentrated on ep-0 and ep-3 of the service.

li: can you paste ipvs state? suspect IPVS hash skew or stale weights.

ajay: posting snippet: ```
# ipvsadm -Ln --stats
TCP  10.20.30.5:443 rr persistent 600
  -> 10.200.1.12:443          Masq    1      0          0
  -> 10.200.1.13:443          Masq    1      7823       130
  -> 10.200.1.14:443          Masq    1      0          0
```

maya: that looks like heavy skew on 10.200.1.13. but weight is 1 for all.

li: check conntrack counts + kernel drop counters on those endpoints. also any MTU mismatch after drain? we swapped host NIC profile on the drained hosts.

ajay: conntrack on ep-3 is unusually high: `conntrack -L | wc -l` ~210k on 10.200.1.13, others ~8k.

sre-oncall: infra-bot shows a netdevice MTU change event during the drain at 02:35 UTC for node gpu-ssd-13: `mtu 9000 -> 1500` — maybe path MTU introduced fragmentation/loss to endpoints.

infra-bot: [event] host gpu-ssd-13: NIC profile switched to smaller MTU due to kernel upgrade compatibility patch.

tess: RDMA workloads on those nodes — did we force fallback to TCP? RDMA failure can cause path behavioral changes.

li: good call. RDMA stack bounces when MTU mismatches. If RDMA ports flapped, traffic might be funneled to fewer healthy endpoints that still accept RDMA/TCP conversions.

maya: also seeing repeated SYN retrans on packet capture from kube-proxy host: ```
# tcpdump -i bond0 host 10.200.1.13 and tcp
07:02:12.123456 IP 10.10.5.8.52344 > 10.200.1.13.443: Flags [S], seq 12345, win 65535, options [mss 1460], length 0
07:02:12.223567 IP 10.10.5.8.52344 > 10.200.1.13.443: Flags [S], seq 12345 (retry)
```

ajay: retries match the service logs. clients time out then fallback to retry middleware which increases load on the few successful endpoints.

li: let's check ipvs hash seed and kernel IPVS version; if the kernel changed on some nodes during drain, hash algorithm can produce different bucket mapping and result in endpoint fan-in.

ajay: kernel on gpu-ssd-13 is 5.15.80, others 5.15.78 before upgrade.

maya: minor patch but could touch netfilter/ipvs. we saw similar in stg earlier.

li: mitigation ideas: 1) temporarily cordon the problematic endpoint(s) from the service (ipvsadm -e or adjust service endpoint list) 2) force kv-cache / conntrack flush on kube-proxy then bounce kube-proxy 3) rollback NIC profile to 9000 MTU on affected host.

tess: rolling a quick cordon for 10.200.1.13 to relieve pressure. doing `kubectl delete pod` for the pod backing that IP — will drain traffic away.

ajay: cordon reduced retries within 3m, but still seeing higher tail on remaining endpoints. conntrack table still heavy.

li: flush conntrack entries for service VIP on the kube-proxy nodes: `sudo conntrack -D -d 10.20.30.5` — that will remove stale mappings. also `ipvsadm -C` on affected kube-proxy to clear IPVS state (careful, will drop in-flight).

maya: doing staged conntrack flush on one proxy at a time to avoid global outage.

sre-oncall: note for postmortem: this was an emergent interaction between NIC MTU change during host kernel upgrade and IPVS hash/conntrack persistence. record rollback and a checklist for draining gpu nodes with RDMA.

ajay: after conntrack flushes and cordon, retries back to baseline in ~7m. file a bug to block MTU profile changes on GPU pools during business hours.

li: followup actions: - ensure kernel IPVS version parity across pool before drain - add a kube-proxy readiness check that validates IPVS bucket distribution skew - add a metric for endpoint conntrack concentration - update drain playbook to preserve MTU for RDMA nodes.

tess: opening infra ticket INF-4672 with logs and remediation steps. attaching tcpdumps and ipvs stats.

maya: thanks team. I'll coordinate config lock for MTU changes and add a small canary for future kernel upgrades. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: [ticket] INF-4672 created by tess — assigned to eng-infra oncall.

sre-oncall: marking incident as resolved for now. we'll run a follow-up postmortem tomorrow.

ajay: adding a note — consider enabling IPVS persistent-conns aging tuning to avoid long-lived bucket stickiness under churn.

li: agreed. will draft PR for a kube-proxy flag and a playbook update.

maya: good work. keeping an eye on us-west1-b for next 24h.

ajay: thanks, closing thread.
